A SIX-SYMBOL BOUNDARY FOR REUSABLE NONLINEAR FAST-FORWARDING
2026-10-31. Locally derived reduction; historical priority not assessed.

This is the concrete next obstruction after CONSTRUCTION.txt. It is not a new
algorithm for discrete logarithms and not a lower bound for the homogeneous
S3 neighboring-product cellular automaton. It concerns polynomial-size explicit
group-operation circuit networks. A conditional computational barrier and an
unconditional linear-representation lower bound are proved below.

1. OPERATION AT ISSUE

Fix the group S3, with six explicitly named symbols. A state has m+1 group
registers. The one-step update is given by a polynomial-size circuit using
group multiplication, inverses, constants and shared subexpressions. Given an
initial state and T in binary, predict one distinguished register after T steps.

The local law is extremely easy to acquire: it has only 36 table entries. Even
granting its exact table for free does not settle the downstream operation.
Unknown representation acquisition is therefore not the bottleneck of this
example. Experimental trajectories still cost their actual number of steps.

Claim A. A classical algorithm for this operation with time polynomial in
m, circuit size and log(1+T) gives a classical polynomial-time algorithm for
discrete logarithms in F_(2^m), for instances supplying an irreducible defining
polynomial and a primitive generator. The reduction uses only O(m) endpoint
queries, and only a yes/no readout of the distinguished register.

Constant pointwise prediction error does not remove the reduction. If a query
returns the correct binary readout with probability at least 2/3, independent
repetitions and majority reduce each error to O(1/m), then a union bound makes
the binary search reliable with polynomial overhead. A numerical scalar
estimate of the deterministic readout with absolute error <1/2 likewise
reveals the bit. No exact full-state output is required.

This is a reduction, not a proof that such an algorithm cannot exist. It does
not assert an exponential classical discrete-log lower bound. Quantum
algorithms and changes to the computation model are outside this classical
comparison.

Research constructor: capability_reframe. 2026-10-31.

STATUS

This file proves a restricted end-to-end mathematical construction and records a
synthetic implementation. It does not establish historical novelty, a measured
physical capability, or the parent's full mission of a genuinely new scientific
power. Its main algebra is standard class-two collection. The useful result of
the investigation is a completely paid baseline: observations -> checked finite
identities -> constructed nonlinear program summaries -> actual binary-horizon
execution. Neither a hidden conjugacy nor a downstream solver is supplied.

The proposed organising principle is: when the observed local operation lies in
a finitely checkable algebraic variety with compact free objects, construct the
free object on the FUTURE INPUT VARIABLES, instead of reconstructing latent
coordinates of the observed alphabet. This can expose a reusable computational
operation that a one-step model by itself does not expose. Here the variety is
groups with central commutators. This principle is not asserted novel.

1. POWER SOUGHT AND STRONG BASELINES

Power: after a finite campaign of noisy experiments on a previously unknown
local rule, compute a full n-site nonlinear system at a binary-encoded horizon
T, for arbitrary future initial states, in work polynomial in n and log T.
The learned object must also support composing future nonlinear local programs.

Retain-and-simulate: learn the q^2 local table and evaluate nT local updates.
Retain all global transitions: q^n states; table squaring is exponential in n.
Cycle detection: up to q^n global states; can be excellent on short cycles and
must be included in a practical benchmark. It is not uniformly polynomial.
Generic learned one-step approximation: local prediction error alone does not
guarantee long-horizon accuracy. A rare wrong table entry can be queried next.
Generic dense quadratic lifting: once appropriate coordinates/closure are
known, a dimension O(n^2) linear system gives binary powering; naive dense
storage O(n^4) and arithmetic O(n^6 log T). Structured lifting is substantially
stronger and may reproduce the present O(n^3 log T) algorithm.
